claim: For the binary limited-magnitude sticky-deletion channel of Wang, Vu, and Tan, define \(E^{\le}_{2,1}(x)\) for \(x\in\{0,1\}^9\) to contain \(x\) and every word obtained by deleting one repeated bit from each of at most two distinct runs, never erasing an entire run. If \(M^{\le}_{2,1}(9)\) is the largest size of a code \(C\subseteq\{0,1\}^9\) whose sets \(E^{\le}_{2,1}(x)\) are pairwise disjoint, then \(M^{\le}_{2,1}(9)=120\). An explicit 120-word code gives the lower bound, while an exact nonnegative rational weight certificate on received words of lengths \(7,8,9\), of total weight \(120\), gives the matching upper bound because every source error ball has weight at least \(1\).
integrity: The lower and upper bounds are supplied as standalone finite certificates. The verifier reconstructs the channel from definitions and checks every source word with exact rational arithmetic; no external solver output is required for the proof.
scientific_limitations: Exact only for the explicitly defined binary length-nine at-most-two-run, magnitude-one channel; no classification of optimum codes and no claim for other lengths.
title: Exact binary length-nine optimum for two magnitude-one sticky deletions
